objects.textPreview: Objective: robot at deployment executing a task in an unseen situation at training
The robot covers the range and precise
Learn how to grasp and move across variations of the same task.
Estimate the current conditions so the policy can use suitable actions.
Working hypothesis: generalizable behavior and useful environmental context support adaptation.
An RL policy conditioned on environment
Standard state describes the robot and task; environmental parameters describe current conditions.
Known in training; estimated at deployment
Training: learn policy weights from reward. Deployment test: keep those weights fixed.
Assumption to test: varied training produces a policy capable of executing at held-out heights.
A controlled visual mass estimate works
Fixed-density cubes provide a visible size-to-mass relationship.
Scope: one material, fixed density and friction, fixed camera. This tests interpolation over size.
The full pipeline runs in simulation
Initial RGB image → mass estimate → supplied policy input → pick-and-lift execution.
3 configured trials · 3 final successes · 50 actions per trial
One seed per size. Integration is demonstrated; estimation benefit and unseen-height adaptation remain untested.
Train pick and lift across object heights
Vary initial object elevation relative to the arm while keeping the task and grasp strategy consistent.
The robot base stays fixed. The object starts at different elevations.
First height study: control mass, friction, object geometry, and required lift clearance.
Deploy at a held-out initial height
Freeze the trained policy and provide environmental context estimated from deployment observations.
Report within-range held-out heights separately from heights beyond the training range.
Current estimator: mass. Estimator target for the height study still needs to be specified.
At each held-out height, compare the same frozen policy under three context inputs.
Can the policy execute at the unseen height?
How much performance is lost to estimation?
Remove true copies of estimated inputs.
What we can say now—and test next
Current evidence supports the components; the proposed comparison must establish adaptation.
2.76 g MAE on held-out cube sizes
Establish policy capability with true context
Evaluate estimated context at held-out heights
Compare against true and fixed inputs
If true context fails: inspect policy capability and task feasibility.
If true context succeeds but estimates fail: inspect estimation and policy sensitivity.
Later stage: revise environmental estimates through interaction, success, and failure.
